syllabus_topics: Introduction: historical perspective on the importance of human-machine interaction in computer engineering.
Paradigm examples of interactive technologies, devices, systems, services, and applications.
The iterative and incremental development process of interactive systems and services.
Idea generation and evaluation: Methods and techniques for prototyping: low, medium, and high fidelity.
Methods and techniques for analyzing users and usage contexts.
Predictive evaluation, heuristic evaluation, and participatory evaluation.
Design and Construction of Visual Interfaces: interaction devices, styles, and technologies.
assessment_rules: For normal evaluation, the final grade is calculated as 0.8 * Average(Bake-off1, Bake-off2) + 0.2 * Max(Average(Mini-test1, Mini-test2), Exam). A minimum grade of 9.5v is required on the final average of the laboratory assessment. The mini-tests grade can be recovered in the normal examination period, using the better score between the mini-test average and the exam. For student workers, the two laboratory projects (bake-offs) have equal weight and account for 100% of the final grade, performed individually. Optionally, student workers can participate in the mini-tests, in which case the normal evaluation calculation (80% + 20%) applies. Special examination period assessment consists of a single project (100%).
bibliography: Manuel J. Fonseca, Pedro Campos, Daniel Gonçalves, Introdução ao Design de Interfaces (3ª Edição), FCA, 2017 (Out.)
Alan Dix et al., Human-Computer Interaction (3rd ed.), Prentice Hall, 2004
Jenny Preece et al., Interaction Design – beyond computer interaction (3rd ed.), John Wiley, 2011
institution: Universidade De Lisboa — LEIC-A Eng. Informática e de Computadores (IST)
degree: Licenciatura em Engenharia Informática e de Computadores - Alameda (LEIC-A)
